claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated on August 18, 2026, that the United States has no talks planned with Iran.
US President Donald Trump posted a map on social media depicting the Strait of Hormuz as US territory.
Crossings through the Strait of Hormuz fell 19.5% to 95 transits last week, according to shipping data platform Kpler.
An unidentified projectile damaged the engine room of a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman, causing a crew casualty.
Major General Amir Hatami, commander of Iran's Artesh army, announced a $30,000 reward for the killing or capture of any US soldier.
Iran has executed 28 political prisoners so far in 2026, according to Iran Human Rights founder Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam.
The United Arab Emirates Defence Ministry reported that its air defences detected two Iranian ballistic missiles, both of which landed in the sea.

Iranian negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that the Strait of Hormuz will remain shut until the US lifts its port blockade and oil sanctions, releases frozen assets, and ends military operations.
Eight air strikes hit the Abu al-Duhur military base in the eastern countryside of Idlib, Syria, causing damage but no casualties.
Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei mocked US President Donald Trump's claims of controlling the Strait of Hormuz on August 18, 2026.
Former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov released a video address on August 18, 2026, calling for a wartime presidential election in Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy formally nominated acting defence minister Yevhen Khmara to permanently assume the post of defence minister.
A drone strike near the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant killed one nuclear specialist and wounded 17 people.
The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed that a drone strike struck staff members of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant at a bus stop.
A Russian strike damaged equipment at a thermal power plant operated by DTEK in central Ukraine, forcing operations to stop.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated on August 18, 2026, that the United Kingdom will continue to support Ukraine 100%.
Russian missile strikes on the village of Pechenihy in northeastern Ukraine killed 10 civilians.
Russian officials reported that Ukrainian forces launched approximately 620 drones towards the Moscow region overnight.
German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider arrived in Kyiv on August 18, 2026, to discuss resilient infrastructure renewal.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced sanctions against International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane and Senior Trial Lawyer Abdoulaye Seye.
Four US human rights groups filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration in a New York court, alleging its campaign to dismantle the ICC is unconstitutional.
Three ICC judges, Kimberly Prost, Solomy Balungi Bossa, and Reine Alapini-Gansou, sued the US administration in a New York federal court in June.
The US sanctions against ICC President Tomoko Akane and Senior Trial Lawyer Abdoulaye Seye freeze their US assets and restrict US entities from transactions with them starting September 17.
The International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant.
The US Treasury Department issued a general licence permitting the wind-down of transactions involving ICC President Tomoko Akane through September 17.
Opening statements began on August 18, 2026, in a federal court in California in a lawsuit brought by a coalition of 29 US states against Meta.
California Deputy Attorney General Megan O'Neill stated in court that Meta designed products to hook users, harvest their data, and hide the truth from the public.
The coalition of states suing Meta is seeking financial penalties of approximately $200 billion.
Meta was previously ordered to pay $942 million in fines in a separate New Mexico lawsuit.
Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg and former Meta employee Arturo Bejar are expected to testify during the California trial.
US President Donald Trump ordered a substantial reduction in joint military exercises with South Korea prior to the start of the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung stated on August 18, 2026, that a firm military alliance with the US underpins South Korea's national security.
The United States maintains approximately 28,500 troops stationed in South Korea.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung renewed calls to accelerate the transfer of wartime operational control (Opcon) of South Korean forces from the United States.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for faster progress on South Korea's nuclear-powered submarine program.
The Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises were scheduled to involve approximately 18,000 South Korean troops along with US forces.
Delhi Police submitted a 42-page affidavit to the Supreme Court late on August 17, 2026, regarding student protests over competitive exams.
Delhi Police reported that on July 20, over 30,000 protesters were faced by 5,000 uniformed police officers.
Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi directed the implementation of a four-tier question paper checking system and new security infrastructure at the National Testing Agency.
The National Testing Agency removed 600 experts as part of an examination team overhaul.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on July 25, 2026, and Pralhad Joshi assumed charge of the ministry.
Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das issued a two-day ultimatum to the Union government to honor commitments regarding the withdrawal of FIRs against student protesters.
The Supreme Court requested Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to furnish details of FIRs against student protesters with a view to quashing them under Article 142.
Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju claimed that no protester was seriously injured or suffered broken bones during the July 20 protest in Delhi.
A Right to Information response stated that 10 people were wounded by pellets during the July 20 protest march in Delhi.
Delhi government's Anti-Corruption Branch arrested former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain in connection with alleged corruption in the Delhi Jal Board tendering process.
The Anti-Corruption Branch arrested five other individuals alongside Satyendar Jain, including former Delhi Jal Board CEO Udit Prakash Rai and former consultant Ankit Srivastava.
Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal asserted that the corruption charges against Satyendar Jain were fake and brought at the behest of the BJP.
Anti-Corruption Branch investigations alleged that Udit Prakash Rai received ₹1.52 crore through AN Enterprises to purchase immovable property.
Aam Aadmi Party leader Manish Sisodia linked Satyendar Jain's arrest to upcoming assembly elections in Punjab.
The Goa government filed an appeal in the Supreme Court seeking to enhance former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal's sentence to life imprisonment.
The Bombay High Court set aside Tarun Tejpal's acquittal on August 6, 2026, and sentenced him to 10 years of imprisonment in a 2013 rape case.
Tarun Tejpal was acquitted by a Goa trial court in May 2021 before the Bombay High Court reversed the decision.
The Goa government's Supreme Court petition challenged the High Court's order allowing Tarun Tejpal's two aggravated rape sentences to run concurrently.
The PM CARES Fund received ₹480 crore in donations in FY 2024-25, representing a 30% drop compared to the previous year.
The PM CARES Fund spent ₹87.85 lakh in FY 2024-25, which amounted to 0.01% of its available closing balance.
The closing balance of the PM CARES Fund reached ₹8,452.06 crore at the end of FY 2024-25.
Audited accounts show ₹7,846 crore of the PM CARES Fund corpus was held in fixed deposits with scheduled banks for FY 2024-25.
The PM CARES Fund received ₹324.66 crore in refunds from implementing agencies during FY 2024-25.
The audited financial statements for PM CARES Fund for FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 were signed by auditors on August 7, 2026, and published on August 17.
